cards.text: Friend, this is Paul, an apostle, writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). In the last chapter he talked about Abraham, who believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness, and Paul says those words were written for us too, who believe in Him who raised Jesus (Romans 4:22-24). Now Paul turns to what that means for us, and he starts with one big word: Therefore.

cards.question: Paul says that since we've been justified through faith, we have what with God?

cards.text: PEACE with God, friend, and Paul says it comes through our Lord Jesus Christ. Me and my oven timer have been at war since the day I moved in, so I'm taking NOTES.

cards.question: Paul says we've gained access into God's grace by working hard enough.

cards.text: Through Jesus, by faith, we've gained access into this grace, and Paul says it's the grace we stand in. Friend, after years lying flat in the back of a drawer, STANDING sounds amazing.

cards.question: Standing in that grace, Paul says we rejoice in the ___ of the glory of God.

cards.text: Then Paul says, not only that. And friend, the next thing he rejoices in is NOT what I'd have put on my list.

cards.question: Not only that, Paul says we also rejoice in what?

cards.text: When my edges went soft and my stamps came out blurry, I did NOT rejoice, friend, I went so quiet in that junk drawer the dust had more to say than me. But Paul gives a reason: we know suffering produces something.

cards.question: Paul says we rejoice in our sufferings because suffering produces ___.

cards.text: And it's a chain, friend, like dough to oven to box, each step making the next. Paul says perseverance produces character.

cards.question: At the end of Paul's chain, character produces hope.

cards.text: In the drawer, every time the light came in we hoped, and most of the time it was just somebody digging for tape. But Paul says THIS hope does not disappoint us.

cards.question: Why does Paul say this hope does not disappoint us?

answers.text: God has poured out His love into our hearts
We have earned it by enduring our hardships
God has taken all suffering out of our lives

cards.question: Paul says God poured out His love into our hearts through whom?

cards.text: POURED out, friend. Not a little sprinkle on top, a full pour, through the Holy Spirit, whom God has given us.
Now Paul looks at when Christ died: at just the right time, while we were still powerless. I know powerless, friend, I spent years in a drawer where my biggest move was rolling over.

cards.question: While we were still powerless, Paul says Christ died for the ___.

cards.text: The UNgodly, friend, which means I'd have made that list with ROOM to spare. Then Paul gets honest about how people usually are.

cards.question: Paul says it's common for someone to die for a righteous man.

cards.text: Very rarely, Paul says, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die. Me, I'd give you my last chocolate chip and then bring it up for a WEEK.

cards.question: So how does Paul say God proves His love for us?

answers.text: Christ died for us while we were still sinners
Christ died for us after we turned our lives around
Christ blessed us after we proved ourselves faithful

cards.text: While we were STILL sinners, friend, not after we got it together, and if God waited on me to get it together, we'd ALL still be waiting. Then Paul says we've now been justified by His blood, and he builds on that with a how much more.

cards.question: Since we've been justified by His blood, Paul says we'll be saved from wrath through Him.

cards.text: Then Paul reminds us where we were: enemies of God. ENEMIES, friend, not "we kind of drifted apart," more like "lose my number."

cards.question: When we were enemies of God, Paul says we were reconciled to Him through what?
Paul says we were reconciled through the Son's ___, so how much more shall we be saved through His ___.

cards.text: Enemies, then reconciled, then saved, and Paul STILL isn't done, because he says, not only that. This man stacks it up like I stack cookie boxes: one more, one more, ONE MORE.

cards.question: To close this part, Paul says we also rejoice in whom, through our Lord Jesus Christ?

cards.text: We rejoice in God through Jesus, the One through whom we've now received reconciliation. And there's that line again, "through our Lord Jesus Christ": Paul opened with it on peace with God, and he closes with it on rejoicing in God.

findings.problem: The setup says the next thing Paul rejoices in is NOT what Papa Dorin would have put on his list. That rules out the wrong answers on card 8. 'Our good deeds' and 'Our own strength' are the kind of things anyone would put on that list, so only 'Our sufferings' fits the hint.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The comparison 'like dough to oven to box, each step making the next' doesn't share the core action of Paul's chain, where each thing produces the next. Dough doesn't make the oven, and the oven doesn't make the box, so the image doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The first sentence joins two sentences with a comma ('I did NOT rejoice, friend, I went so quiet in that junk drawer...'). Counting that, the card has three sentences, which is more than a story card after the opening is allowed.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence is a run-on that strings three clauses together with commas and 'and': the 5:8 emphasis, 'not after we got it together' and the joke. Add the 5:9 setup and the card works out to more than two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Blank 1 ('death') asks again for the fact card 10 just tested ('The death of His Son', Romans 5:10). Only blank 2 ('life') is new.
findings.question: Is it okay for a choice card to test again an answer from the card right before it? Or should a fill in the blank card with two blanks test only new content, for example by changing this card to a single blank for 'life'?
